claims.text: The composition root is the one place where the application's objects are wired together; in Đơn Hàng it is Program.cs together with the AddDonHangInfrastructure method it calls.
claims.source_hint: glossary composition-root; outline item 1; examples/don-hang @ stage-2: STAGE.md (Program.cs: the composition root)

claims.text: At stage-2 Program.cs calls builder.Services.AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString, redisConfiguration, smtp) and then builder.Services.AddScoped<OrderService>(); it does not name EfOrderRepository.

AddDonHangInfrastructure is declared in DonHang.Infrastructure (ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs) and registers DonHangDbContext and the adapters behind the core's ports, such as IOrderRepository -> EfOrderRepository.
At stage-2 DonHang.Api.csproj has ProjectReferences to DonHang.Domain and DonHang.Infrastructure; DonHang.Domain.csproj has no ProjectReference.

To call a public method declared in another project of the solution, a project adds a ProjectReference to it; that reference also lets every class in the project name the other project's public types.
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: MSBuild ProjectReference item; C# accessibility (public types across assemblies)

claims.text: At stage-2 ProductsController's constructor takes (DonHangDbContext db, IProductRepository products); List starts its query from db.Products; the comment above the class says the list has no rule to apply, only a query to shape.
DonHangDbContext is EF Core's DbContext for Đơn Hàng's database: it derives from DbContext and lives in DonHang.Infrastructure.

At stage-2 OrdersController takes OrderService and the ports IOrderRepository, ICustomerRepository; Create/Cancel/Ship call OrderService, Get/List call IOrderRepository; it never names DonHangDbContext; in Controllers only ProductsController.cs does.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Api/Controllers/OrdersController.cs:13-17; git grep DonHangDbContext -- DonHang.Api/Controllers

claims.text: The DI container holds the registrations and creates objects while the application runs; the composition root is the code where the registrations are written (IServiceCollection calls in Program.cs and AddDonHangInfrastructure).
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Dependency injection (service registration in Program.cs, IServiceProvider resolves services)

claims.text: An arrow between DonHang.Api and DonHang.Infrastructure runs between two projects outside the core and does not break the dependency rule, which is about what DonHang.Domain names.

A rule added to ProductsController.List would sit in a driving adapter, outside the core and out of reach of unit tests driving OrderService; skipping the core suits a read with no rule; once an endpoint has a rule, the core keeps it in one place.
Opposing view: some teams send every endpoint through the core so there is one path to learn; that pays off when many people add endpoints and rules appear often.

At stage-2 git grep -n -e "AddDonHangInfrastructure" -e "AddScoped<OrderService>" -- DonHang.Api DonHang.Infrastructure prints three lines (Program.cs:26, 27; ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs:14); git grep -n "DonHangDbContext" -- DonHang.Api/Controllers prints two (ProductsController.cs:11, 15).
